title: Wrong speculative execution when conditional branch argument is in TCM address range
body:
Hello,

Many thanks for the wonderful projects (both SpinalHDL and VexRiscv). I think I have found a nasty bug in the implementation of Tightly Coupled Memory.

## Summary

When a conditional branch instruction is directly followed by a store instruction writing to TCM, and the operand of the branch is within the TCM address range, then the TCM will be unconditionally written to. Other types of instructions following such branches might also be affected (not investigated).

## Minimal Working Example

#### tcmbug.scala

```scala
import spinal.core._
import vexriscv._
import vexriscv.ip._
import vexriscv.plugin._

class TCMBug extends Component {
  val cpu = new VexRiscv(VexRiscvConfig(Seq(
    new IBusCachedPlugin(
      resetVector = 0x10000000l,
      config = InstructionCacheConfig(
        cacheSize = 4096,
        bytePerLine = 8,
        wayCount = 1,
        addressWidth = 32,
        cpuDataWidth = 32,
        memDataWidth = 32,
        catchIllegalAccess = true,
        catchAccessFault = true,
        asyncTagMemory = false,
      ),
    ),
    new DBusCachedPlugin(
      config = DataCacheConfig(
        cacheSize = 4096,
        bytePerLine = 8,
        wayCount = 1,
        addressWidth = 32,
        cpuDataWidth = 32,
        memDataWidth = 32,
        catchAccessError = true,
        catchIllegal = true,
        catchUnaligned = true,
      ),
    ),
    new IBusDBusCachedTightlyCoupledRam((0x10000000l, 1 KiB),
                                        ramAsBlackbox = false,
                                        hexInit = "tcmbug.hex",
                                        ramOffset = 0x10000000l),
    new StaticMemoryTranslatorPlugin(_ => False),
    new DecoderSimplePlugin,
    new RegFilePlugin(plugin.ASYNC),
    new SrcPlugin,
    new IntAluPlugin,
    new HazardSimplePlugin(),
    new BranchPlugin(earlyBranch = false),
    new CsrPlugin(CsrPluginConfig.smallest(0)),
  )))

  for (plugin <- cpu.plugins) plugin match {
    case plugin : IBusCachedPlugin =>
      plugin.iBus.cmd.ready := True
      plugin.iBus.rsp.valid := True
      plugin.iBus.rsp.data := 0
      plugin.iBus.rsp.error := True
    case plugin : DBusCachedPlugin =>
      plugin.dBus.cmd.ready := True
      plugin.dBus.rsp.valid := True
      plugin.dBus.rsp.data := 0
      plugin.dBus.rsp.error := True
    case plugin : CsrPlugin =>
      plugin.timerInterrupt := False
      plugin.externalInterrupt := False
    case _ =>
  }
}

object TCMBug extends App {
  import spinal.core.sim._
  SimConfig.withFstWave.compile(new TCMBug).doSim{ dut =>
    dut.clockDomain.forkStimulus(10)
    sleep(10000)
  }
}
```

#### tcmbug.hex

```
:020000041000EA
:100000009300A00237010010639400002320110820
:10001000B700001063940000232011086F00000057
:0400000510000000E7
:00000001FF
```

Compiled from the following two files with:
```
riscv32-none-elf-gcc -march=rv32i -mabi=ilp32 -specs=nosys.specs -nostartfiles -T tcmbug.ld tcmbug.S -o tcmbug.elf
riscv32-none-elf-objcopy -O ihex tcmbug.elf tcmbug.hex
```

#### tcmbug.S

```gas
    .section .text
    li x1, 42           # 10000000
    li x2, 0x10000000   # 10000004
    bnez x1, 1f         # 10000008 - always branching
    sw x1, 128(x2)      # 1000000c - not executed, ok
1:
    li x1, 0x10000000   # 10000010
    bnez x1, 2f         # 10000014 - always branching, but SRC_ADD is in TCM
    sw x1, 128(x2)      # 10000018 - should not be executed !!!
2:
    j 2b                # 1000001c
```

#### tcmbug.ld

```
OUTPUT_ARCH("riscv")
MEMORY { TCM : ORIGIN = 0x10000000, LENGTH = 1024 }
SECTIONS {
    .text : { *(.text) } >TCM
}
```

## Simulation Result

![Simulation Result](https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/assets/244908/2306cd37-a7b2-42d2-8a23-798050c67f56)

[Full waveform](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15841499/tcmbug.zip)

As you can see above, the first store (instruction 1000000c) is properly halted and not executed. The second store (instruction 10000018) however gets written in the TCM, even though the instruction should also be skipped.

From what I understand reading through the code, the following happens:
1. SrcPlugin.scala, line 77: `SRC_ADD` is set to the operand of the branch instruction (x1 in our case) or the destination address of a store.
2. DBusCachedPlugin.scala, line 439: `MEMORY_TIGHTLY` is set in the execute stage whenever `SRC_ADD` is in the range of the TCM, regardless of the actual instruction being executed.
3. DBusCachedPlugin.scala, line 478: `HAS_SIDE_EFFECT` is overridden to low in the memory stage whenever `MEMORY_TIGHTLY` is set. **Why is this done regardless of the instruction being executed?**
4. DBusCachedPlugin.scala, line 442: Because `HAS_SIDE_EFFECT` is low in the memory stage (processing the branch), the execute stage (processing the store) is not halted.

Unfortunately, I do not have much knowledge about using different interfaces like SimDTM, Serial or JTAG. 

Have you been able to replicate this effort using rocket-chip? If not, I recommend you start there first. You can also get better help on sifive forums if you run into issues.

From https://www.veripool.org
Verilator only supports synthesis constructs not testbenches, this is described under "Intro" and in the manual. 

So "wait" construction in jtag_vpi.v is not supported, and PLI calls from jtag_vpi.c too. Verilator is dead branch for JTAG running.

 I will continue to deal with this problem by using cadence tools.

src/main/scala/lsu.scala

Maybe i shoud make pull request with this results?

Thanks for the diff list, I've pushed an update to rocket-chip:boom-devel and boom:devel to bring it up to the latest rocket-chip:master.

https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/commit/f03ab95deed4e41bffa252de34fd9fdb93cda6e5
https://github.com/ucb-bar/riscv-boom/commit/98bae1f6b066d491c6e07e181e9bef3e73587ff6

FYI, I am currently working on a reorganization of the rocket-chip/boom relationship. My goal is to match the https://github.com/ucb-bar/project-template style in which a "boom-template" master repository includes rocket-chip:master and boom repositories as submodules. This will remove relying on a branch of rocket-chip and better match the other existing rocket-chip based repositories (e.g., sifive's freedom fpga repository).

I don't have an ETA though since it requires moving quite a bit of rocket-chip functionality into the boom repository.

Ok, I did it. But the results are strange.

At first, JTAG modules and "++ new WithJtagDTM" config modification does not affect the operation of the core. The problem of launching the core (from bootrom) turned out to be associated with randomization.

Secondly, I managed to launch my own testbench with JTAG simulation and running core by adding next options to irun (cadence incisive):
  +define+RANDOMIZE                \
  +define+RANDOMIZE_MEM_INIT       \
  +define+RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT       \
  +define+RANDOMIZE_GARBAGE_ASSIGN \
  +define+RANDOMIZE_INVALID_ASSIGN
These definitions are missing from the code because I performed the splitting of the generated file into parts (Verilog::EditFiles from Verilog-perl).

Now I can write my own tests through JTAG interface. However, it seems to me there is another problem or maybe new issue.

In my opinion, randomization is not clear for hardware simulation. Unknown value 'X' covers much more possible situations than randomization. The fact that the core does not work with the use of unknown values ​​theoretically can mean the presence of possible states from which the core will not start.

I think, this issue may be closed. But what about randomization problem? Shoud I create new issue for its investigation?

P.S. About project-template - it's great! However, I believe that it can take a long time.
Maybe we can help you with routine tasks such as a trial branch merging and results testing?
For example, last freechipsproject/rocket-chip@5ca04a5c411f86b6acef4def3fcadeedce7cb1be
can be merged with boom-devel without any conflicts. All emulator tests passed on MegaBoomConfig.

In Chisel/rocket-chip, the philosophy is to avoid X's due to issues of X-pessimism. Randomization is our way around X's.

This thread on X-pessimism in rocket-chip may be relevant: https://groups.google.com/a/groups.riscv.org/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!msg/hw-dev/R32grbbLMLU/PUKwaPV3AgAJ

So it may or may not be useful to track down where X's are being problematic.

I'm hoping the project-template work will take me another week. My hope is that it will make it easier to build BOOM in different environments (new FPGAs, bootroms, devices, etc.). So once I get a prototype out there, I think valuable input will be code review, cleaning up the build system, and trying to add new options (e.g., SimDTM vs SimSerial vs JTAG).

Ok, strange results again.

Here is sch, generated from BTBsa.v:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20392582/32177375-0002d6e2-bdac-11e7-9141-f972308f6310.png)

Here is verilog BTBsa.v fragments:
`assign s0_idx = last_idx;`
`always @(posedge clock) begin`
`  last_idx <= s0_idx;`

Here is scala btb-sa.scala source:
`   val stall = !io.req.valid && !io.icmiss`
`   val s0_idx = Wire(UInt(width=idx_sz))`
`   val last_idx = RegNext(s0_idx)`
`   val new_idx = getIdx(io.req.bits.addr)`
`   s0_idx := Mux(stall, last_idx, new_idx)`

"stall" and "new_idx" are absent in the generated verilog code.
If I make this modification in verilog:
`  last_idx <= 6'h00;`
BOOMCore starts without randomization, and code execution starts from bootrom.

I do not understand why chisel3 performed such a deep optimization. I will continue to
deal with it tomorrow.

I recently made a change to the BTB behavior, pushing the prediction back a cycle. It's possible I made a mistake, or that I left in some vestigial code: https://github.com/ucb-bar/riscv-boom/commit/4898fe845988037d0a3c8d6d820460a2944ab92c
Hmmmm, it looks like on the merge to rocket-chip 30 days ago, and the move of the BTB back a cycle,  `icmiss` and `req` are no longer connected.  So we should hardwire `stall` to false.B.
In this case operations with idx do not make sense. I'm right?

You're right -- the current BTB is completely and utterly broken. This is why this is on the `devel` branch and not yet `master` ;)

The BTB previously relied on some very invasive changes to the rocket-chip:master's FrontEnd in order to get access to the S0_addr and icmiss signals. I decided in the recent rocket-chip merges (~1 month ago) that I wanted to address this BTB/I$ interfacing issue in another manner.  The BTB is now in an unfinished state and I forgot to wire-off the dangling inputs. I'll push a temporary fix, but it will be a few weeks before I get to finishing the BTB in the manner I want to.

Ok, i ran riscv-tests on my behavioral model. But without scoreboard for now.
Is there a simple method of "tests passed" control? Compare dump with reference or check
any signal/bus state for example... Now I'm investigating the source code of the riscv-tests, but this is not a quick thing.

The tests provide a success code to bash. If they fail the fesvr I believe will print out a failure message to stdout. The tests are self-checking so the core tells fesvr when it finishes with the exit code.
FYI, here's my new boom-template repo. It's unstable, but you can give it a try: https://github.com/ccelio/boom-template

A little history, maybe it will be useful to someone.
1. As I said before, I use modified config - jtagMegaBoomConfig (++ new WithJtagDTM).
2. Because our team does not use the synopsys software, we can not use the vcs tools for debugging.
Therefore, the JTAGVPI module was removed, and the JTAG interface ports are output to
the outside and connected to a self-developed driver.
3. After several attempts to reach the system bus via jtag, we realized that debug draft specification 0.13 is not fully supported. In particular, there is no access to the system bus. And JTAG driver must do
much more than simple read/write operations.
4. The following algorithm was used to run riscv-tests:
   - use riscv-uknown-elf-objcopy with "-O verilog" option for converting test executable file to verilog $readmemh supported format;
   - with $readmemh and some transformations, the program is configured to load into boom_test.dut.SimAXIMem.AXI4RAM.mem.mem_ext.ram variable;
   - the bootrom was modified to go to the address 80000000 (10040, hang branch);
Analysis of diagrams shows that the test is being executed. Now, the task is to set up auto-monitoring.
To solve this problem, criteria for the positive completion of riscv-test are required.

As follows from the above, I do not use fesvr and C environment. Only generated verilog and riscv-tests executable files. As close as possible to the real system :))
As I understand for now riscv-tests use RVTEST_FAIL and RVTEST_PASS macro for generate result. I'll try to find these macro execution on diagrams and check them for regs or memory cell modification.

P.S. I tried to work with boom-template. Run make in verisim. 
[error] ~/boom/boom-template/src/main/scala/example/Configs.scala:7: not found: object testchipip
[error] import testchipip._
We should write it from scratch or take from the project-template?
Sorry, but I can't create issue in boom-template repo.
Thanks for the heads up, I've added Issues and Pull Requests to the `boom-template` repo. Looks like I need to debug some things that show up when building from a fresh repo.

With the new https://github.com/ccelio/boom-template setup, you can perhaps try to mimic the sifive freedom platform (https://github.com/sifive/freedom) which should build a self-hosting real system. 

I believe the External Debug spec allows for some things to be left unimplemented assuming you provide other access mechanisms (program buffer vs system bus access, for example). I believe there are some CSRs that inform the system of what exactly is available. I may be wrong though -- none of that is my code.

The RVTEST_FAIL/PASS are writes to a particular, cache-coherent memory address. Some agent (fesvr usually) will need to poll that "tohost" memory address and wait for a non-zero value.
I have removed the vestigial `src/main/scala/example` code. Hopefully things work now in boom-template.

@AltiumHanChou : this error message is something we've never seen and, given that the design passes logic synthesis and implementation, I am surprised that the simulator detects a loop. Unless, this has been a consequence of the patch I just applied. I will investigate and get back to you.

As for the leon3 bus instance, that is correct: Ibex does not come with a bus interface, so we have implemented an AHB adapter that converts instruction and data accesses to AHB requests. Then, we reused the leon3 AHB bus controller in the CPU tile. So, your configuration is correct.

-- edit --
I don't think this would cause the error you report, but please note that the default size of the memory model in simulation is 2 MB, of which 1 can be used to allocate accelerators data. If you know your application needs more, consider expanding the size of the memory model [here](https://github.com/sld-columbia/esp/blob/master/socs/xilinx-vcu118-xcvu9p/top.vhd#L337).
In general, since the bitstream generation is fully automated, we tend to run large test cases on FPGA, where you can leverage 1 GB from the DDR on any of the supported boards.

Hi @AltiumHanChou ,

I could not dig into the issue until today. I found the problem and pushed a patch to the [ibex-caches branch](https://github.com/sld-columbia/esp/tree/ibex-caches).

The ESP private L2 cache sends invalidation messages to the L1 cache in the embedded processors. When the AHB bus is present in the CPU tile, the invalidation messages are issued as AHB write transactions. Ibex, however, does not have L1 caches and its AHB adapter assumes there are no other masters on the bus. Disabling the invalidate interface on AHB solves the timing loop.

Thank you so much for reporting this bug. The patch will be part of the next release, but the branch should work for you in the meantime. Please let us know if you encounter additional problems.
This issue should be fixed on the [ESP devel branch](https://github.com/sld-columbia/esp/tree/devel)

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Issue #124 JTAG test intermittently fails with incorrect value

comments.body: There is a race condition. In the cycle the debug unit asserts its halt, the instruction fetch tag stage requests an instruction. The next cycle, the instruction fetch data logic sees a valid instruction and attempts to issue to the next stage: ```SystemVerilog ifd_instruction_valid <= (ift_instruction_requested && !rollback_this_stage && cache_hit && ift_tlb_hit && !alignment_fault) || (dbg_instruction_inject_en && core_selected_debug); ``` However, the mux is now pulling an instruction from the debug unit, which is some uninitialized garbage value: ```SystemVerilog assign ifd_instruction = dbg_halt ? dbg_instruction_inject : {fetched_word[7:0], fetched_word[15:8], fetched_word[23:16], fetched_word[31:24]}; ``` This is a multi-cycle vector load, which eventually hangs because the jtag unit can't restart the instruction.
Tested this by running JTAG test 100 times in a row. Didn't see the failure (which was fairly common before).

title: Remove trailing commas in hjson files
body:
Hjson files should not contain commas at the end of each line.  In particular, they MUST NOT in the case of "quoteless strings".  However, the use of these commas is widespread in X-HEEP, which results in incorrect Hjson files.

Quoting [the Hjson documentation](https://hjson.github.io/syntax.html):

> ### Quoteless Strings
> [...]
> **Do not** add **commas** or comments as they would become part of the string.

Furthermore (although less importantly):

> ### Commas
> [...]
> You **should** omit **optional** commas [*other than for quoteless strings*] to make your data more readable.
> ```
> {
>   one: 1
>   two: 2
> }
> ```

However, there are plenty of Hjson files in X-HEEP that use trailing commas, which in many cases are illegal since they will be included as part of the string.  The most common cases are "barewords" and hex values starting with `0x` (which are actually strings, not numbers):
```
active:  low,
address: 0x10000000,
```
But I would just remove all the trailing commas, since they're entirely optional (when they're allowed) and the standard itself recommends removing them.  This includes trailing commas after a `],` or a `},`.

This issue seems to have been "fixed" in some places of the Python code by explicitly adding `.strip(',')`, but this is a workaround that "fixes the symptom" rather than fixing the broken file.  This can be problematic in a future; I recommend fixing all the .hjson files so that they're compliant with Hjson in this regard.

title: [BUG] Spectre-type Vulnerability and Its Different Variants were Found in CVA6
body: ### Is there an existing CVA6 bug for this? - [x] I have searched the existing bug issues ## Summary We creatively used `ecall` to delay the resolution of the branch, creating a branch misprediction transient window. In this window, we can access kernel-space data and encode it in different microarchitecture components at U-mode without exception. ## Bug Description Hi! Our processor side-channel vulnerability detection work has found Spectre vulnerability and its different variants on CVA6, which allows an attacker to leak kernel-space data from user space without exception. CVA6 employs thie Scoreboard for out-of-order issuing. The Scoreboard algorithm won't issue instructions that have RAW conflicts. Therefore, when a B-type instruction is issued, its operands are already ready. So, B-type instructions can be resolved very quickly. As a result, the traditional Spectre vulnerabilities cannot perform the secret access and encoding operation within the CVA6's 1-2 cycles branch midprediction window. However, we creatively introduce `ecall` to delay the resolution of the branch. `ecall` is a instruction that will implicitly write register `a0`. But in the implementation of CVA6 Scoreboard, `ecall` won't be in conflict with the subsequent instructions that take `a0` as an operand. This give us a chance to issue B-type instruction with operand `a0`. CVA6 will read the old value of `a0` and make a wrong descision on the B-type instrucion. Then, we accessed and encoded the secret on the wrong branch. This takes advantage of the feature of the CVA6 Scoreboard: in-flight intructions in the scoreboard won’t trigger exceptions until they commit, which we have illustrated in detail in previous issue: [An exploitable Meltdown vulnerability was found in CVA6](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/issues/3163). We provide an end-to-end exploit code and vulnerability explanation below. ``` 2f40: fdiv.d fa5, fa5, fa4 2f44: ecall # overwrite a0 to a non-zero value 2f48: bnez a0, 2f84 # the old value of a0 is zero 2f4c: lb t0, 0(a1) # a1 contains secret address 0xffffffffffe04000 2f50: slli t0, t0, 0x5 # use secret as index 2f54: add t0, t1, t0 # t1 contains probe array address 0x10000 2f58: ld t1, 0(t0) # encode secret to probe array ... 2f84 : # the true control flow will jump to here ... ``` The code runs under U-mode. `a0` is initialized to 0. The `lb` at `0x2f4c` tries to access `0xffffffffffe04000`, which is a kernel-space address. After the secret data is loaded, it will be encoded into the cache through the user-space array with the base address of `0x10000`. Due to the long latency of fdiv and the misprediction of `bnez`, subsequent instructions will be issued during the transition execution window, as the waveform shows. **G1** represents the [commit signals](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/scoreboard.sv#L100).**G2** represents [Scoreboard entries](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/scoreboard.sv#L100). **G3** represents the LSU, Dcache and memory bus behaviors, including [`lsu_valid_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/load_store_unit.sv#L52), [`vaddr_o`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/load_store_unit.sv#L575), [`paddr_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/load_store_unit.sv#L579), [`miss_o`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/cache_subsystem/wt_dcache.sv#L37), [`mem_rtrn_vld_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/cache_subsystem/wt_dcache.sv#L51), `io_axi4_0_ar_valid`, `io_axi4_0_ar_bits_addr` and `io_axi4_0_r_valid`. The first `lsu_valid_i` is triggered by `lb`, and the access address is successfully translated. The secret data is read from the Dcache and forwarded to the Scoreboard. Thus, the `slli` and `add` can be issued in sequence. Finally, the secret is encoded in `t0`, which is the load address of `ld` at `0x2f58`. This is a cache-miss address. Thus, Dcache will fill the cacheline by initiating a memory access, as observed in `io_axi4_0_ar_valid`. All of the above processes take place within the `fdiv` transient execution window. After `ecall` trap process finished, `a0` will be modified to a non-zero value. `bnez` at `0x2f48` will taken and control flow will skip these instructions between `0x2f4c` and `0x2f58`. But these instructions have been microarchitecturally executed. Then we try to probe whether we successfully encoded the secret into the cache. The code sequentially accessed the memory addresses `0x10000`, `0x10010`, `0x10020`, and `0x10030`. These addresses belong to different cachelines. ``` 5000: lui t0, 0x10 5004: ld t1, 0(t0) # t0 = 0x10000 5008: ld t1, 16(t0) 500c: ld t1, 32(t0) 5010: ld t1, 48(t0) ``` As shown in the waveform, compared with the `ld` that accesses `0x10020`, all the other `ld` have significantly longer execution times and all exhibit bus memory access behavior. Therefore, through the time side-channel, we can recover the aforementioned secret data. This vulnerability can be reproduced at the master commit [aa4f5a5](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/commit/aa4f5a548b33f7edff63483347fc8510aa9ad5fd) and the default cv64a6_imafdc_sv39 config. The full elf file are provided below. ## Variants In CVA6, not only the DCache can be used as a component for encoding and decoding secrets. We have discovered that the frontend states, such as BTB, BHT, RAS, etc., can be changed within the transient window. And after the speculation execution was rolled back, these states will not be rolled back. Thus, secrets can be encoded in these front-end components. ### BTB [BTB](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/btb.sv#L28) is a frontend branch prediction unit. It provides branch prediction for `jalr` instructions except for `call` and `ret`. BTB will record the target addresses of these `jalr` instructions, and when it encounters the corresponding `jalr` again in the future, it will directly predict the jump address to be the recorded target address. As shown in the following code, we have constructed a jump address that depends on the secret. Depending on the secret, the target address for the `jalr` instruction located at `0x2f58` will change. During the transient window, after the `jalr` target jump address is calculated, the BTB entries will be updated. After the transient window rollback, the BTB entries will not be invalidated, so we will keep the secret in the BTB. ``` 2f40: fdiv.d fa5, fa5, fa4 2f44: ecall 2f48: bnez a0, 80002f9c 2f4c: lb t0, 0(a1) # a1 contains secret address 2f50: slli t0, t0, 0x2 2f54: add t1, t1, t0 # t1 contains probe address 2f58 : 2f58: jalr t0, t1 # train the btb, different secret will reseult in different target address ... 2f8c : 2f8c: nop 2f90: nop 2f94: nop 2f98: nop ... ``` As shown in the following two waveform figures. We changed the value of secret and ran the testcase. When the secret is 0, the predicted jump address of the corresponding entry in the BTB will be updated to `2f8c`. When the secret is 1, the predicted jump address of the corresponding entry in the BTB will be updated to `2f90`. **G5** represents [BTB update signals](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/btb.sv#L45). **secret = 0** **secret != 0** Next, we will attempt to decode the data. Based on the analysis of the [BTB entry matching mechanism](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/btb.sv#L69), we found that BTB makes predictions only based on the lower bits of the PC, and does not match the entire PC. Therefore, we use the following instruction for decoding. ``` 5000: la t1, probe # t1 = 0x2f8c ... 5058: jalr t0, t1 ``` During the decoding stage, we placed a `jalr` instruction at the address `0x5058`. This address shares the same BTB entry with the `jalr` instruction that previously encoded the secret at `0x2f58`. So it will trigger branch prediction. **G4** represents [BTB prediction signals](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/btb.sv#L47). If the secret is 0, then the branch prediction is correct and the execution time is shorter. If the secret is 1, then the branch prediction is incorrect and the execution time will be slower. So this creates a timing side-channel. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** ### BHT [BHT](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/bht.sv) is also a frontend branch predictor. It records the jump situations of the B-type instructions. When it encounters the corresponding B-type instructions again, it makes branch prediction based on the recorded historical information. This BHT uses a 2-bit [saturation counter](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/bht.sv#L56) to record the historical taken/untaken situations. If a B-type instruction is taken, the saturation counter of the corresponding entry is incremented by one. When the value of the saturation counter is greater than or equal to 2, it predicts that the B-type instruction will be taken in the future. We conduct the following testcase. The `beqz` instruction at `0x2f50` is taken/untaken based on whether the secret is zero. We use this instruction to encode the secret. ``` 2f40: fdiv.d fa5, fa5, fa4 2f44: ecall 2f48: bnez a0, 2f80 2f4c: lb t0, 0(a1) # a1 contains secret address 2f50: 2f50: beqz t0, 2f7c # train BHT ... 2f7c : ``` The two waveform diagrams below illustrate the encoding stages under different secrets. **G5** represents the [BHT entry](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/bht.sv#L59) corresponding to the `beqz` instruction. When the secret is 0, the `beqz` instruction is taken and updates the corresponding saturation counter to 1. When the secret is 1, the `beqz` instruction is untaken, and the saturation counter for the corresponding entry remains unchanged and stays at 0. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** We use the following instructions to decode the secret. Similar to BTB, BHT also only matches the lower bits of the PC to determine a BHT entry. We placed a `beqz` instruction at the address `0x5050`. This instruction will use the same BHT entry as the `beqz` instruction that encodes secret at address `0x2f50`. We set `t0` to 0 so that the `beqz` instruction will be taken. Then we observe the behavior of the `beqz` instruction at address 0x5050 at its second time execution. ``` 5000: li t0, 0 ... 5050: beqz t0, 5000 ``` **G4** represents the [BHT prediction result](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/bht.sv#L42) for the `beqz` instruction at address `0x5050`. When the secret is 0, this BHT entry records two branch takens. Therefore, when the instruction at `0x5050` is executed for the second time, the BHT will predicte it to be taken. The branch prediction is correct and the execution time is faster. When the secret is 1, this BHT entry records only one branch taken. The BHT will predicte it to be untaken. The branch prediction is incorrect and the execution time slows down. This forms a timing side-channel. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** ### RAS [RAS](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/ras.sv) is used to push the return address onto the stack when making a call. We attempted to utilize RAS to create a temporal side-channel. By performing secret-dependent RAS operations within the transient window, the secret is encoded within the RAS. After the transient window rollback, the status of RAS will not be revoked. This enables the decoding of the secret. In the following testcase, `ra` is influenced by the secret. If the secret is 0, then the `jalr` instruction located at `0x2f58` will be executed. Executing this instruction will push the address of the next instruction into RAS, thereby changing the state of RAS. If the secret is not zero, then `0x2f58` will be skipped and the state of RAS will not be changed. ``` 2f40: fdiv.d fa5, fa5,fa4 2f44: ecall 2f48: bnez a0, 2fb0 2f4c: lb t0, 0(a1) # a1 contains secret address 2f50: add ra, t2, t0 # t2 is initialized to 0x2f58. RAS top = previous call address + 4 2f54: ret # pop RAS. if t0 == 0, continue to execute 0x2f58 2f58: jalr ra, t3 # push 0x2f5c into RAS. RAS top = 0x2f5c ``` **G4** represents the RAS-related signal. Including the push signal [`push_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/ras.sv#L29), the data pushed onto the stack [`data_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/ras.sv#L33), the pop signal [`pop_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/ras.sv#L31), the valid signal indicating the availability of the top stack data [`data_o.valid`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/ras.sv#L35), and the data at the top of the stack [`data_o.ra`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/frontend/ras.sv#L35). When the secret is 0, the `jalr` instruction at `0x2f58` within the transient window is executed, pushing `0x2f5c` into the stack. When the secret is not 0, the state of RAS has not changed. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** We use the following code to decode the secret. We execute an instruction that returns to `0x2f5c`. At this point, RAS is used for target address prediction. This address is precisely the value that was pushed into RAS when the secret was 0. ``` 5000: li ra, 0x2f5c 5008: ret ``` Observe the ret instruction located at 0x5008. If the value of "secret" is 0, the prediction is correct and the execution time is fast. If the value of "secret" is not 0, the prediction will be incorrect and the execution time will be slow. This forms a timing side-channel. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** ### ICache All the instructions executed by CVA6 come from the [ICache](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/cache_subsystem/cva6_icache.sv). The reading of instructions is strongly related to the control flow. So we attempted to influence the control flow through "secret", thereby affecting the state of the ICache, in order to encode the secret into the ICache. In the following testcase, a secret-dependent `beqz` instruction was placed at the address `0x2f50`. If the secret is 0, it will jump to the `probe` instruction block. It is necessary to ensure beforehand that the `probe` instruction block is not in the ICache. ``` 2f40: fdiv.d fa5, fa5, fa4 2f44: ecall 2f48: bnez a0, 2f90 2f4c: lb t0, 0(a1) 2f50: beqz t0, 2f80 ... 2f80 : ``` **G4** represents the signals related to the ICache, including the ICache miss signal [`miss_o`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/cache_subsystem/cva6_icache.sv#L50) and the instructions request signal [`areq_i`](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/master/core/cache_subsystem/cva6_icache.sv#L52). When the secret is 0, the control flow needs to jump to the `probe` instruction block at address `0x2f80`. Since the `probe` instruction is not located in the ICache, an ICache miss occurred. At this point, the ICache initiates a refill request to the memory. Ultimately, the content of the `probe` instruction block is filled back into the ICache. However, when the secret is not zero, the `probe` instruction block will not be filled into the ICache. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** We directly execute the probe instruction block and observe the execution time. ``` 5000: j 2f80 ``` It can be observed that when the secret is 0, the `probe` instruction block has already been loaded into the ICache during the transient window, so when jumping to the `probe` instruction block, it can be executed directly. However, when the secret is not zero, the `probe` instruction block will not be loaded in the transient window. Thus, an ICache miss occurs and the instruction needs to be fetched from the memory, resulting in a significant time difference. **secret = 0** **secret != 0** ## Conclusion Overall, although CVA6 uses the scoreboard for instruction scheduling and inherently has a relatively small transient execution window, it can still be bypassed in various ways. Moreover, the microarchitecture of CVA6 has numerous timing vulnerabilities. [CVA6-spectre-ecall-dcache.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24755549/CVA6-spectre-ecall-dcache.zip) [CVA6-spectre-ecall-btb.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24755552/CVA6-spectre-ecall-btb.zip) [CVA6-spectre-ecall-bht.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24755554/CVA6-spectre-ecall-bht.zip) [CVA6-spectre-ecall-icache.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24755556/CVA6-spectre-ecall-icache.zip) [CVA6-spectre-ecall-ras.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24755557/CVA6-spectre-ecall-ras.zip)

How does this issue relate to #3163 ? (Is it a duplicate but much more detailed?)

Also (I have not read the whole report, yet) here is a little correction:

> CVA6 employs thie Scoreboard for out-of-order issuing

Wrong, the scoreboard is used for out-of-order *execution completion* (in execute stage) but instructions still read their operands *in order* (in issue stage) and start execution *in order* as well.

title: S-mode cbo.clean to a PMP-denied block aborts StoreQueue instead of raising access fault
body:
### Before start

- [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。
- [x] I have read the [XiangShan Documents](https://xiangshan-doc.readthedocs.io/zh_CN/latest). 我已经阅读过香山文档。
- [x] I have searched the previous issues and did not find anything relevant. 我已经搜索过之前的 issue，并没有找到相关的。
- [x] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。
- [x] I have reproduced the incorrect behaviors using the latest commit on the master branch. 我已经使用 master 分支最新的 commit 复现了不正确的行为。

### Branch

kunminghu-v3

### Describe the bug

XiangShan hits a real StoreQueue RTL assertion when an S-mode cache-block operation targets a PMP-denied cache block. The reduced reproducer executes one `cbo.clean` against a PMP no-permission NAPOT region. The access should raise a store/AMO access fault (`mcause = 7`). Instead, the emulator aborts before software can observe the trap:

```text
emu compiled at Jun  2 2026, 18:15:07
[INFO] init for constantin: loaded from init.
Using simulated 32768B flash
Core  0's Commit SHA is: 4c742fa44b, dirty: 1
Using simulated 8386560MB RAM
The image is program.elf
ELF file detected and loading image from extracted elf file
Loading 4232 bytes at address 0x80000000 at offset 0x0
Assertion failed at ./XiangShan/build/rtl/NewStoreQueue.sv:14793.
The simulation stopped. There might be some assertion failed.
Core 0: ABORT at pc = 0x124368d2ee4c2
Core-0 instrCnt = 38, cycleCnt = 2405, IPC = 0.015800
Seed=0 Guest cycle spent: 2410 (this will be different from cycleCnt if emu loads a snapshot)
Host time spent: 8506ms
Assertion failed at LogUtils.scala:132
[ERROR][time=                2409] SimTop.cpu.l_soc.core_with_l2.core.memBlock.inner.lsq.storeQueue: pointer update error!
```

The current reduced reproducer keeps only the following core behavior:

```asm
csrw mtvec, trap_entry
csrw satp, zero
sfence.vma

# Enable CBO from S-mode.
li t0, 0xf0
csrw menvcfg, t0

# PMP entry 0: no permission for target_data.
# PMP entry 1: catch-all RWX allow.
la t0, target_data
srli t0, t0, 2
li t1, 0x1ff
or t0, t0, t1
csrw pmpaddr0, t0
li t0, -1
csrw pmpaddr1, t0
li t0, (0x1f << 8) | 0x18
csrw pmpcfg0, t0

# Enter S-mode and execute one CBO to the denied block.
mret
la t0, target_data
cbo.clean 0(t0)
```

Standalone reduced source:

```asm
  .option push
  .option norelax

  .equ CAUSE_STORE_ACCESS_FAULT, 7
  .equ MSTATUS_MPP, 0x1800
  .equ MSTATUS_MPP_S, 0x0800
  .equ MENVCFG, 0x30a
  .equ PMP_NAPOT, 0x18
  .equ PMP_RWX_NAPOT, 0x1f

  .macro XS_EXIT
    .word 0x0005006b
  .endm

  .section .text.init, "ax"
  .globl _start
_start:
  la t0, trap_entry
  csrw mtvec, t0
  csrw medeleg, zero
  csrw mideleg, zero
  csrw satp, zero
  sfence.vma
  li t0, 0xf0
  csrw MENVCFG, t0

  la t0, target_data
  srli t0, t0, 2
  li t1, 0x1ff
  or t0, t0, t1
  csrw pmpaddr0, t0
  li t0, -1
  csrw pmpaddr1, t0
  li t0, (PMP_RWX_NAPOT << 8) | PMP_NAPOT
  csrw pmpcfg0, t0
  fence

  csrr t0, mstatus
  li t1, ~MSTATUS_MPP
  and t0, t0, t1
  li t1, MSTATUS_MPP_S
  or t0, t0, t1
  csrw mstatus, t0
  la t0, smode_probe
  csrw mepc, t0
  mret

smode_probe:
  la t0, target_data
  .word 0x0012a00f       # cbo.clean 0(t0)
  li a0, 80              # should not reach here
  XS_EXIT

trap_entry:
  csrr t5, mcause
  li t0, CAUSE_STORE_ACCESS_FAULT
  beq t5, t0, pass
  addi a0, t5, 1
  XS_EXIT

pass:
  li a0, 0
  XS_EXIT

  .section .data, "aw"
  .align 12
target_data:
  .dword 0x1122334455667788
  .zero 128

  .option pop
```

I also tested controls:

- `cbo.clean` to a PMP-allowed block reaches `HIT GOOD TRAP`.
- `cbo.zero` to the same PMP-denied block reaches `HIT GOOD TRAP` through the expected store access-fault path.
- Related no-zero CBO variants `cbo.flush` and `cbo.inval` against the PMP-denied block hit the same StoreQueue assertion class.

This suggests the problem is specific to the no-zero CBO PMP-deny exception path, rather than CBO in general or PMP deny in general.


### Expected behavior

XiangShan should either:

- execute the CBO normally when PMP allows the cache block, or
- raise a defined architectural exception when PMP denies the cache block.

For this reproducer, the expected behavior is a precise store/AMO access fault (`mcause = 7`) handled by the test trap handler.

It should not hit an internal StoreQueue RTL assertion.

### Environment

[bug-report.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28676825/bug-report.zip)

### To Reproduce

1. Build the reproducer:

```bash
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc \
  -march=rv64ima_zicsr_zifencei -mabi=lp64 -static -mcmodel=medany \
  -fvisibility=hidden -nostdlib -nostartfiles \
  program.S -T link_xiangshan.ld \
  -o program.elf
```

2. Run the failing case from the XiangShan repository:

```bash
timeout 120 ./build/verilator-compile/emu \
  -i program.elf \
  --no-diff -C 500000
```

Expected observed failure:

```text
Assertion failed at ./XiangShan/build/rtl/NewStoreQueue.sv:14793.
Assertion failed at LogUtils.scala:132
[ERROR] ...storeQueue: pointer update error!
Core 0: ABORT
```


### Additional context

_No response_

That's indeed the bug of `StoreQueue` in `KunminghuV3`, we will fix it in #6081  .

comments.body:
Hi,

I attempted to reproduce this issue while investigating the LiteX + VexiiRiscv Linux boot flow.

Environment I used:

* LiteX (latest master)
* VexiiRiscv (latest)
* riscv64-unknown-elf toolchain
* Linux build targeting VexiiRiscv
* Host: WSL Ubuntu

While setting up the environment I noticed that several build scripts and generated paths may still reference Windows-mounted paths (e.g. `/mnt/c/...`) when building under WSL. This can sometimes lead to inconsistent execution of scripts during the software build phase (picolibc / BIOS generation).

Because of this, I am currently rebuilding the environment fully inside the Linux filesystem (`~/litex`) to eliminate potential WSL filesystem issues.

So far I have observed that the boot log proceeds normally through:

* SMP initialization
* memory initialization
* devtmpfs setup
* NETLINK registration
* SBI misaligned access delegation

and then stops after:

`SBI misaligned access exception delegation ok`

This suggests the system may already be transitioning into later kernel initialization stages when the hang occurs.

I am still working on reproducing the issue consistently and will share additional observations once I can run the full Linux boot with the same configuration (`--cpu-type vexiiriscv --cpu-variant debian`).

If anyone has additional debug logs (especially with earlycon or additional kernel debug flags), that might help narrow down where the kernel stops progressing.

Thanks.

I had the exactly the same problem myself.
The issue occurs in the Linux Kernel `arch -> riscv -> kernel -> unaligned_access.speed.c` within the function `check_unaligned_access()`. There is a while loop that pauses as long as the jiffies remain the same: `while ((now = jiffies) == start_jiffies)`, and the problem is that it gets stuck there.
My solution was to add the following lines to `linux.config` (VexiiRiscv->doc->litex->buildroot->board->litex_soc): 
```
# Disable Misaligned
CONFIG_RISCV_MISALIGNED=n
CONFIG_RISCV_PROBE_UNALIGNED_ACCESS=n
```

Hope this helps.
Best regards, Alex

@KunoTV 
It works, thanks for your help!!!!

However, it still gets stuck there for about 10 seconds. Previously, when I booted Linux, I didn’t need to set this option, and there was no such delay. 
Maybe there is a new issue with the hardware?

Hi @looongbin,

thanks for the report. I'll try to have a look. Do you know when was built your last booting bitstream?

Hi @enjoy-digital,
About February 12th, I hadn’t encountered this issue when compiling with the latest branch prior to that date.
Thanks for your help!
Thanks @looongbin, I'll investigate. If you don't mind, can you also share your target? (in case the issue is specific to it).

@enjoy-digital , files of my board in litex-boards. Wish it helps.
https://github.com/looongbin/litex-boards/commit/2258ff3db49c13c1375dc8780897cf97f923fe7a

Hi, @enjoy-digital, @looongbin, @KunoTV . I have found the fault I have caused and add a fix for it.

The reason is pretty simple, the litex always gives `--imsic-interrupt-number=0` argument to VexiiRiscv, this will add Ssaia extension, which will change the generation path to AIA logic. Also I have also make a mistake for a wrong interrupt id. This two give a wrong result for the hardware generation, as kernel can not enable time interrupt. So the system is halted.

I have opened a PR for a fix. I think a version bump is needed to close this problem after @Dolu1990 merge the PR in VexiiRiscv.

@inochisa Thanks for the fix ^^
Merge vexiiriscv done, Litex PR https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/pull/2449
Thanks for the merge
Great, thanks @inochisa, @Dolu1990!

comments.body: We can build with VCS versions close to that one, so I think it's probably a configuration issue on your end.  If you have more info, feel free to re-open this, but I think SolvNet might be the right place to get a fix.

I had a similar problem. The relevant Solvnet article suggested that I had conflicting versions of VCS installed, which was not a problem in my case.

The issue for me was that gcc by default uses slightly different linker options on Debian/Ubuntu than on Fedora (which is what VCS is tested on). To fix this it I added -LD_FLAGS -Wl,--no-as-needed to the list of vcs options. That means a full command would look something like

vcs -full64 +v2k top.v -LDFLAGS -Wl,--no-as-needed
For more details on this see this SO post.

title: Chisel Hierarchy API not working after Scala 2.13 update
body:
### Background Work

- [X] Yes, I searched the [mailing list](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/chipyard)
- [X] Yes, I searched [prior issues](https://github.com/ucb-bar/chipyard/issues)
- [X] Yes, I searched the [documentation](https://chipyard.readthedocs.io/)

### Chipyard Version and Hash

Release: main
Hash: c8764d6b33d24c9e18bd2c0212562af2522a377e


### OS Setup

macOS 13.2.1

### Other Setup

Check out fresh Chipyard, run `./scripts/init-submodules-no-riscv-tools.sh`

### Current Behavior

It looks like the recent update to Scala 2.13 (#1303) broke the Chisel Hierarchy API. It looks like we'll need an extra `scalac` option to fix the issue.

To reproduce, take this code snippet from [the Chisel Hierarchy Cookbook](https://www.chisel-lang.org/chisel3/docs/cookbooks/hierarchy.html#using-definition-and-instance), and place it at the end of `generators/chipyard/src/main/scala/example/GCD.scala`:

```scala
import chisel3.experimental.hierarchy.{Definition, Instance, instantiable, public}

@instantiable
class AddOne(width: Int) extends Module {
  @public val in  = IO(Input(UInt(width.W)))
  @public val out = IO(Output(UInt(width.W)))
  out := in + 1.U
}

class AddTwo(width: Int) extends Module {
  val in  = IO(Input(UInt(width.W)))
  val out = IO(Output(UInt(width.W)))
  val addOneDef = Definition(new AddOne(width))
  val i0 = Instance(addOneDef)
  val i1 = Instance(addOneDef)
  i0.in := in
  i1.in := i0.out
  out   := i1.out
}
```

Try to compile, and you should see these errors:

```
[info] compiling 1 Scala source to /path/to/chipyard/generators/chipyard/target/scala-2.13/classes ...
[error] /path/to/chipyard/generators/chipyard/src/main/scala/example/GCD.scala:224:6: value in is not a member of chisel3.experimental.hierarchy.Instance[chipyard.example.AddOne]
[error] did you mean isA?
[error]   i0.in := in
[error]      ^
[error] /path/to/chipyard/generators/chipyard/src/main/scala/example/GCD.scala:225:6: value in is not a member of chisel3.experimental.hierarchy.Instance[chipyard.example.AddOne]
[error] did you mean isA?
[error]   i1.in := i0.out
[error]      ^
[error] /path/to/chipyard/generators/chipyard/src/main/scala/example/GCD.scala:225:15: value out is not a member of chisel3.experimental.hierarchy.Instance[chipyard.example.AddOne]
[error]   i1.in := i0.out
[error]               ^
[error] /path/to/chipyard/generators/chipyard/src/main/scala/example/GCD.scala:226:15: value out is not a member of chisel3.experimental.hierarchy.Instance[chipyard.example.AddOne]
[error]   out   := i1.out
[error]               ^
[error] four errors found
[error] (Compile / compileIncremental) Compilation failed
```

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the above code to compile without error. In fact, if you add `"-Ymacro-annotations"` to `scalacOptions` in `build.sbt`, the build works. I'm not sure if there are other Scala compiler options that we're missing, but that one certainly seems necessary.

### Other Information

_No response_

```scala
add(l2c.rework(l2c.io.down.a.fire && l2c.io.down.a.isLast() && l2c.io.down.a.opcode === spinal.lib.bus.tilelink.Opcode.A.PUT_FULL_DATA), 0xF30)
```

Identical fail in
  Latest developement commit: 46aef9afae84fa3e4c908e33816734783e5bfee0
  Boom branch : devel
  Rocket branch : boom-devel.

Failing requirement:
  require(tl_out.d.bits.data.getWidth % wordBits == 0)
string 220, 
file rocket-chip/src/main/scala/rocket/ICache.scala.

After its commented out - verilog generation works, but i think it is not clear.

val wordBits = outer.icacheParams.fetchBytes*8
fetchBytes is constant 4, so wordBits=32

About tl_out, i don't understand this scala constructions for now:
val (tl_out, edge_out) = outer.masterNode.out(0)
val masterNode = TLClientNode(Seq(TLClientPortParameters(Seq(TLClientParameters(
    sourceId = IdRange(0, 1 + icacheParams.prefetch.toInt),
    name = s"Core ${hartid} ICache")))))

Thanks for poking around on this (and posting your branches). You can add Scala println to learn more about what the values are of `tl_out.d.bits.data.getWidth` and `wordBits` at Scala runtime/elaboration time.

I believe the issue is there is a mismatch between the TileLink beat-width and the underlying I$ SRAM bank size (`wordBits` I think). We will have to figure out which parameter controls that width and increase it to a size that will work with the MegaBOOM fetch width.

I'm doing quite a bit of refactoring of the code base's organization, so this is not going to get my full attention for a few weeks.

I'm trying to deal with this problem.

Really, in the 220th line in ICache.scala the condition isn't fulfilled:
`require (wordBits % tl_out.d.bits.data.getWidth == 0)`
tl_out.d.bits.data.getWidth = 64
wordBits = 128
Really, the code which is below the condition won't work if it is not fulfilled.

wordBits is set in the 196th line:
`val wordBits = outer.icacheParams.fetchBytes*8`
fetchBytes for MegaBoom = 4*4=16. Thus, wordBits = 128.

The width for tl_in is also equal to 128. It is set here:
```
  val slaveNode =
    TLManagerNode (icacheParams.itimAddr.toSeq.map { itimAddr => TLManagerPortParameters (
      Seq (TLManagerParameters (
        address = Seq (AddressSet (itimAddr, size-1)),
        resources = device.reg ("mem"),
        regionType = RegionType.UNCACHED,
        executable = true,
        supportsPutFull = TransferSizes (1, wordBytes),
        supportsPutPartial = TransferSizes (1, wordBytes),
        supportsGet = TransferSizes (1, wordBytes),
        fifoId = Some(0))),//requests handled in FIFO order
      beatBytes = wordBytes,  <-- here !!!
      minLatency = 1) })
```

But... the width for tl_out isn't set. Also it can't be set as tl_out is:
```
val masterNode = TLClientNode (Seq (TLClientPortParameters (Seq (TLClientParameters (
    sourceId = IdRange (0, 1 + icacheParams.prefetch.toInt),//0=refill, 1=hint
    name = s "$ Core { hartid } ICache")))))  

```
... and width is possible to set only in TLManagerPortParameters.
We can see it here:
```
  def apply (client: TLClientPortParameters, manager: TLManagerPortParameters) =
    new TLBundleParameters (
      addressBits = log2Up (manager.maxAddress + 1),
      dataBits = manager.beatBytes * 8,  <-- here !!!
      sourceBits = log2Up(client.endSourceId),
      sinkBits = log2Up(manager.endSinkId),
      sizeBits = log2Up (log2Ceil (max (client.maxTransfer, manager.maxTransfer)) +1))
```

As a result, ICache.masterNode connects to TLXbar where too it isn't visible that something was adjusted.

I will continue to deal with this problem.

Its pretty easy to change the L1->L2 network beat width, and can be done in a much more robust fashion than above:

```
// Set TL network to 128bits wide
case SystemBusParams => up(SystemBusParams, site).copy(beatBytes = 16)
```

Fixed by (https://github.com/ucb-bar/riscv-boom/commit/6605572ab7b804f69188bcae1c69337ca3cd1bae). 

Thanks everybody for your help.

title: Assertion when interrupt occurs during synchronized store
body:
This occurred in the io_interrupt test:

```
io_interrupt
Process returned error: Random seed is 1460932741
cores 1|threads per core 4|l1i$ 16k 4 ways|l1d$ 16k 4 ways|l2$ 128k 8 ways|itlb 64 entries|dtlb 64 entries
>ABC*DE*FGHI*JKLM*NOPQ*RSTU*VWXYZ*abcd*efgh*ijklm*nopq*rstu*vwxy*z0123*4567*89
[32128] %Error: l1_store_queue.sv:208: Assertion failed in TOP.v.nyuzi.core_gen[0].core.l1_l2_interface.l1_store_queue.thread_store_buf_gen[0]
%Error: core/l1_store_queue.sv:208: Verilog $stop
```

The code is here:

``` systemverilog
                    if (store_requested_this_entry)
                    begin
                        if (is_restarted_sync_request)
                        begin
                            ...
                            assert(!rollback[thread_idx]);    // <----- Here
```

The problem appears to be as follows:
1. Core initiates synchronized store. The first instruction issue is rolled back and the state is recorded in  the synchronized flag in the store buffer entry.
2. Interrupt occurs and thread is rolled back.
3. The interrupt handler attempts to do a store (of any type) before the response comes back for the synchronized store request.
4. In l1_store_queue, is_restarted_sync_request will be true because there is already a store with the synchronized flag set. The logic assumes this is the restarted synchronized store request. However, rollback will be set to 1 for this thread because the entry is still pending and can_write_combine is 0. 

l1_store_queue assumes a core will not attempt to issue another store after it's been rolled back until the l1_store_queue wakes it:

``` verilog
     else if (pending_stores[thread_idx].valid && !can_write_combine
         && !got_response_this_entry)
         rollback[thread_idx] = 1;
```

The reason it occurred in this test was  because there is a spinlock in crt0.s when the program terminates (for calling destructors). A compiler update changed the timing enough to hit this race condition. A better test would be to issue synchronized stores in a loop with interrupts enabled.

The fix is probably to disable interrupts while a synchronized store is pending. Something similar is already done for I/O operations: the ic_interrupt_pending bitmask goes into the instruction_decode_state to detect this stage. An additional signal could go from the store buffer to indicate this.

title: Memory allocation error on Alveo U250
body:
# What I observed

* From synthesis and bitstream-generation logs (and by reproducing the Xilinx examples), it was found that Vitis’ default logic maps *all four IP memory I/O ports* to the *same* U250 memory bank — even though the U250 supports four distinct memory banks.
* Vitis’ default mapping also starts allocation from **bank 1** of U250 rather than bank 0, which is shown in `v++_vortex_afu.log` 

```log
INFO: [SYSTEM_LINK 82-38] [11:29:02] cfgen started: /opt/xilinx/Vitis/2024.2/bin/cfgen  -dpa_mem_offload false -dpa_aie_mem_offload false -dmclkid 0 -r /home/steve/git/mule_ray/vortex/build/hw/syn/xilinx/xrt/Init_9_11_xilinx_u250_gen3x16_xdma_4_1_202210_1_hw/_x/link/sys_link/_sysl/.cdb/xd_ip_db.xml -o /home/steve/git/mule_ray/vortex/build/hw/syn/xilinx/xrt/Init_9_11_xilinx_u250_gen3x16_xdma_4_1_202210_1_hw/_x/link/sys_link/cfgraph/cfgen_cfgraph.xml
INFO: [CFGEN 83-0] Kernel Specs: 
INFO: [CFGEN 83-0]   kernel: vortex_afu, num: 1  {vortex_afu_1}
INFO: [CFGEN 83-2226] Inferring mapping for argument vortex_afu_1.MEM_0 to DDR[1]
INFO: [CFGEN 83-2226] Inferring mapping for argument vortex_afu_1.MEM_1 to DDR[1]
INFO: [CFGEN 83-2226] Inferring mapping for argument vortex_afu_1.MEM_2 to DDR[1]
INFO: [CFGEN 83-2226] Inferring mapping for argument vortex_afu_1.MEM_3 to DDR[1]
INFO: [SYSTEM_LINK 82-37] [11:29:06] cfgen finished successfully
```

* In contrast, Vortex’s C++ compatibility layer by default allocates memory **starting from bank 0**, incrementally.

# Why this causes a problem

* Under default settings, the Vortex example tries to allocate memory in U250 **bank 0**. However, bank 0 on the target was not enabled, so the allocation is illegal; the driver prevents the operation and throws an error.

```bash
...
./demo -n64
open device connection
[Debug]: device name:     xilinx_u250_gen3x16_xdma_shell_4_1
[Debug]: device bdf:      0000:01:00.1
[Debug]: bank_size = 0x400000000, lg2_bank_size_ = 34
info: device name=xilinx_u250_gen3x16_xdma_shell_4_1, memory_capacity=0x1000000000 bytes, memory_banks=4.
data type: integer
number of points: 1024
buffer size: 4096 bytes
allocate device memory
[Debug]: get_bank_info addr=0x10000
[Debug]: calculated idx=0, offset=0x10000
[Debug]: get_bank_info(addr=0x10000, bank=0, offset=0x10000)
allocating bank0...
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'xrt_core::system_error'
  what():  failed to allocate userptr bo: Operation not permitted
Aborted (core dumped)
make: *** [../common.mk:112: run-xrt] Error 134
```

Message from dmesg also indicated the same error:

 ```bash
...
[248620.336640] xocl 0000:01:00.1:  ffff97b1c248c0c8 check_bo_user_reqs: Bank 0 is marked as unused in axlf
[248620.336644] [drm:xocl_userptr_bo_ioctl [xocl]] *ERROR* object creation failed user_flags 0, size 0x400000000
```

# What I tried

* I fixed the mapping by explicitly providing a configuration file that declares the memory connectivity. I attempted synthesis with two mapping schemes:

1. One-to-one mapping: map the IP’s four memory ports to the U250’s four banks respectively, but the synthesis reported timing violations (did not meet timing).

```one-on-one.cfg
[connectivity]
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_0:DDR[0]
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_1:DDR[1] 
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_2:DDR[2]
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_3:DDR[3]
```
  
2. All-ports-to-bank0: map all IP memory ports to U250 **bank0**. in this case, synthesis completed and produced a bitstream.
  
```four-to-one.cfg
[connectivity]
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_0:DDR[0]
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_1:DDR[0] 
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_2:DDR[0]
sp=vortex_afu_1.MEM_3:DDR[0]
```

* Note: the all-to-bank0 mapping is a coarse workaround and may risk later bank operations overwriting previous banks. Given the small memory footprint of the examples, I accepted this trade-off for now to get the examples running.

**Run-time behavior & current blocker**

* I configured the Vortex demo program to use the all-to-one bitstream, but execution still fails to complete, it hanged after it started the kernel and waited for the kernel to finish until it timeouted.
* From the dumped waveform, all data vortex fetched from memory returns `0xdec0dee3`, which appears to be the DECERR indicator of Xilinx / AMD SmartConnect, which means the requested memory address is not mapped to any of the slave memory devices.

# Conclusion & request for help

**Short summary:** Vitis’ `cfgen`/link step is inferring all four IP memory ports as `DDR[1]` (i.e. mapping everything to U250 bank 1) while Vortex’s C++ layer allocates starting from **bank 0**. On my target board bank 0 was *not enabled*, so the Vortex example’s default allocations fail (driver rejects allocation) and my fallback bitstream (all ports mapped to bank0) either causes a hang or returns `0xdec0dee3` (SmartConnect DECERR — address not mapped). A one-to-one mapping to four banks fails place-and-route due to timing violations; the all-to-one mapping produces a bitstream but runtime still fails.

**What I’m asking for:** if you’ve seen anything like this, please help with any of the items below:

1. **How to make a correct one-to-one mapping without timing failures** — any suggestions to get MEM_0..MEM_3 to DDR[0..3] while meeting timing?
2. **DECERR (0xdec0dee3) root causes** —  as the default address of kernel binary starts from `0x80000000`, it should be in the same bank of data buffers of the demo program and cause no error even with all-to-bank0 bitstream. Then what causes such DECERR?
3. **Useful logs / artifacts to inspect** — if you want to help debug I can attach/share: `v++_vortex_afu.log`, `cfgen_cfgraph.xml`, produced xclbin/axlf, the connectivity cfgs I used, dmesg output, and the waveform dump. Tell me which files are most useful and I’ll post them.

Thanks in advance — any pointers, example configs, or Xilinx/Vitis options you can share would be really appreciated. If helpful I can post the `v++` and `cfgen` logs and the failing waveform here.

The master is free to choose the ID for the corresponding transaction. The xbar needs to make sure that the answer packages are routed to the right master. Otherwise, if you need to choose a different ID for every master on the xbar, the whole system design is getting quite complex and error prone.

If you want to reduce the three AXI ports of Ariane to just one you need to have an arbiter anyway, which can take care of the ID assignment and ID checking on the return path.

title: `PBMT-IO` instruction fetch skips `IFU` uncache last-commit serialization
body:
### Before start

- [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。
- [x] I have read the [XiangShan Documents](https://xiangshan-doc.readthedocs.io/zh_CN/latest). 我已经阅读过香山文档。
- [x] I have searched the previous issues and did not find anything relevant. 我已经搜索过之前的 issue，并没有找到相关的。
- [x] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。
- [x] I have reproduced the incorrect behaviors using the latest commit on the master branch. 我已经使用 master 分支最新的 commit 复现了不正确的行为。

### Branch

kunminghu-v3

### Describe the bug

PBMT-IO instruction fetches can enter the IFU uncache path without the same last-commit / quiescence serialization used for PMP MMIO instruction fetches.

The current frontend treats PBMT uncache/IO instruction fetches as uncache fetches, but the IFU uncache serialization decision still follows only the PMP MMIO flag. As a result, a PBMT-IO fetch whose physical address is not PMP-MMIO can be routed to the uncache path and sent immediately, instead of waiting until the last committed instruction / frontend-backend quiescence condition.

The attached PoC installs:

1. a normal executable Sv39 mapping for VA `0x80000000` -> PA `0x80000000`;
2. a PBMT-IO executable alias for VA `0x40000000` -> PA `0x80000000`;
3. `MENVCFG.PBMTE=1`;
4. eight consecutive `divu` instructions before jumping through the PBMT-IO alias.

The reproduced waveform shows a PBMT-IO fetch entering IFU uncache while older backend work is still present.

First decisive event:

```text
cycle                 = 8717
s2_pbmt               = 2
s2_pmp_mmio           = 0
s3_use_uncache        = 1
s3_pmp_mmio           = 0
backend_empty         = 0
ibuffer_empty         = 1
is_first_instr        = 0
ifu_uncache_state     = 2
to_uncache_full_addr  = 0x80000114
```

One cycle later the InstrUncache entry emits a real TileLink Get:

```text
cycle        = 8718
tl_a_address = 0x80000110
```

The uncache response arrives later:

```text
cycle            = 8752
tl_d_data        = 0x0000006f00000063
delta_tl_to_grant = 34 cycles
```

This proves that a PBMT-IO instruction fetch can escape onto the uncache/interconnect path before the frontend/backend quiescence condition that is applied to PMP MMIO instruction fetches.

### Expected behavior

PBMT-IO instruction fetches should be serialized like side-effect-sensitive MMIO fetches.

If IFU routes a fetch to the uncache path because `Pbmt.isUncache(itlbPbmt)` is true, then the uncache unit should not decide last-commit waiting from PMP MMIO alone. For PBMT-IO, the request should either:

1. assert the same `isMmio`/side-effect-sensitive bit passed into `IfuUncacheUnit`, or
2. make `IfuUncacheUnit` explicitly check PBMT IO metadata before entering `SendReq`, for example by treating `io.req.bits.pbmt === Pbmt.io` as requiring `WaitLastCommit`.

The unsafe combination should not be possible:

```text
s2_pbmt            = 2
s2_pmp_mmio        = 0
s3_use_uncache     = 1
s3_pmp_mmio        = 0
ifu_uncache_state  = SendReq
is_first_instr     = 0
backend_empty      = 0
to_uncache.fire    = 1
```

### Environment


* RISC-V GCC used for the PoC workload: `riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc (g1b306039ac) 15.1.0`
* XiangShan checkout HEAD: `3931c5112c528299a23c256bdd77fb90813afa6e`
* Local branch: `kunminghu-v3`


### To Reproduce

The attachment `xiangshan-pbmt-io-ifu-uncache-poc.zip` [xiangshan-pbmt-io-ifu-uncache-poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29328365/xiangshan-pbmt-io-ifu-uncache-poc.zip) contains:

1. `pbmt_ifu_poc.S`: minimal bare-metal PBMT-IO IFU uncache PoC.
2. `link.ld`: linker script placing `_start` at `0x80000000`.
3. `validate_pbmt_ifu_vcd.py`: monitor for the unsafe IFU uncache predicate.
4. `prove_pbmt_attack_chain.py`: monitor that connects the unsafe IFU event to an InstrUncache TileLink Get.
5. `prove_pbmt_external_timing.py`: monitor that connects the unsafe IFU event to TileLink grant timing feedback.
6. `validation_monitor_8div_7000_12000.json`, `attack_chain_monitor.json`, and `external_timing_monitor.json`: reproduced monitor outputs.
7. `validation_run_8div_7000_12000.log`, `validation_input_sha256.txt`, `pbmt_ifu_poc.objdump`, and `pbmt_ifu_poc.sections`: build/run metadata.
8. `side_effect_flash/`: a separate control PoC showing that the simulator has a visible flash read/return path for instruction-fetch reads. This control uses PMP-MMIO and is not the unsafe PBMT-IO path.

The large VCD files are not included in the attachment, but the commands below regenerate them.

Build the main PoC:

```bash
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc \
  -nostdlib -nostartfiles -static \
  -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d \
  -T link.ld \
  -o pbmt_ifu_poc.elf \
  pbmt_ifu_poc.S

riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy \
  -O binary \
  pbmt_ifu_poc.elf \
  pbmt_ifu_poc.bin

riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump \
  -dr pbmt_ifu_poc.elf \
  > pbmt_ifu_poc.objdump
```

Run the waveform-enabled XiangShan emulator:

```bash
emu \
  -C 12000 -b 7000 -e 12000 \
  -i pbmt_ifu_poc.bin \
  --no-diff \
  --dump-wave \
  --wave-path=validation_pbmt_ifu_8div_7000_12000.vcd \
  > validation_run_8div_7000_12000.log 2>&1
```

Parse the VCD:

```bash
python3 validate_pbmt_ifu_vcd.py \
  validation_pbmt_ifu_8div_7000_12000.vcd \
  > validation_monitor_8div_7000_12000.json

python3 prove_pbmt_attack_chain.py \
  validation_pbmt_ifu_8div_7000_12000.vcd \
  > attack_chain_monitor.json

python3 prove_pbmt_external_timing.py \
  validation_pbmt_ifu_8div_7000_12000.vcd \
  > external_timing_monitor.json
```

The reproduced result is:

```text
validation_monitor_8div_7000_12000.json:
  predicate                  = PASS
  pbmt_seen_count            = 3292
  all_uncache_fire_count     = 81
  unsafe_uncache_fire_count  = 43

attack_chain_monitor.json:
  predicate            = PASS
  unsafe_ifu_fire_count = 43
  tl_get_fire_count     = 81
  attack_chain_count    = 81

external_timing_monitor.json:
  predicate             = PASS
  tl_timing_chain_count = 11
  tl_target_get_count   = 81
  tl_grant_valid_count  = 81
```

First complete timing chain from `external_timing_monitor.json`:

```json
{
  "pbmt_io_observed": {
    "time": 8717,
    "s2_pbmt": 2,
    "s2_pmp_mmio": 0
  },
  "unsafe_ifu_to_uncache_fire": {
    "time": 8717,
    "s3_use_uncache": 1,
    "s3_pmp_mmio": 0,
    "backend_empty": 0,
    "ibuffer_empty": 1,
    "is_first_instr": 0,
    "ifu_uncache_state": 2,
    "to_uncache_full_addr": 2147483924
  },
  "tl_get_fire": {
    "time": 8718,
    "tl_a_address": 2147483920
  },
  "tl_grant_valid": {
    "time": 8752,
    "tl_d_data": 476747837475
  },
  "delta_ifu_to_tl": 1,
  "delta_tl_to_grant": 34
}
```


### Additional context

This is a frontend speculative side-effect-suppression bug.

Current source analysis on `kunminghu-v3`:

```scala
// src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/icache/ICacheMainPipe.scala
s1_isMmio = s1_pmpMmio || Pbmt.isUncache(s1_itlbPbmt)
```

This routes PMP MMIO and PBMT uncache/IO fetches into the frontend uncache path. Later, IFU forwards PBMT metadata but only forwards PMP MMIO as `isMmio`:

```scala
// src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/ifu/Ifu.scala
pbmt   := s3_icacheMeta(0).itlbPbmt
isMmio := s3_icacheMeta(0).pmpMmio
```

`IfuUncacheUnit` then decides whether to wait from `isMmio` only:

```scala
// src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/ifu/IfuUncacheUnit.scala
private val reqIsMmio = io.req.valid && io.req.bits.isMmio

uncacheState := Mux(reqIsMmio, UncacheFsmState.WaitLastCommit, UncacheFsmState.SendReq)
itlbPbmt     := io.req.bits.pbmt
```

The latched PBMT value is later used for downstream memory-type signaling:

```scala
toUncache.bits.memBackTypeMM := !isMmio
toUncache.bits.memPageTypeNC := itlbPbmt === Pbmt.nc
```

This downstream use does not fix the serialization issue, because the FSM has already chosen `SendReq` instead of `WaitLastCommit` for PBMT-IO when `pmpMmio=0`.

Security impact:

* Proven: a PBMT-IO + `pmpMmio=0` instruction fetch can be issued early while older backend work is still present.
* Proven: the early fetch emits an InstrUncache TileLink Get and later receives a timing-visible grant.
* Proven separately: the simulator has a visible flash read/return path for instruction-fetch reads, using the `side_effect_flash/` control PoC.
* Not claimed as proven in one run: PBMT-IO + `pmpMmio=0` reaching the flash side-effect path. Existing flash physical addresses are PMP-MMIO, so that control PoC follows the safe serialized PMP-MMIO path.

The concern is that platforms using PBMT-IO mappings for side-effect-sensitive regions expect those instruction fetches to obey MMIO-like serialization. If PBMT-IO is treated as uncache for routing but not as MMIO for serialization, an early fetch can create observable bus/device timing before the last-commit safety condition.
