Hello, it seems that I've managed to find a reason for this failure - I generated VCD traces for the litex simulation, analyzed them in gtkwave and here is what I found.

This is a part of disassembled `bios.bin`:
```
0000254c <litex_putc>:
   ...
   ...
    2562:	37ed                	jal	254c <litex_putc>
    2564:	40b2                	lw	ra,12(sp)
    2566:	8522                	mv	a0,s0
    2568:	4422                	lw	s0,8(sp)
    256a:	0141                	addi	sp,sp,16
    256c:	8082                	ret
```
During execution of this part of code a strange bug happens - at some point the CPU is executing `jal` instruction, but for some reason it saves 2566 as a return address instead of 2564. This results in omitting ` lw    ra,12(sp)`  instruction after we return from the function call. This `lw` instruction is responsible for restoring the return address of the caller function, but since it is not executed, the 2566 value is still left in `ra` register. Therefore, executing `ret` later on results in jumping to 2566 and we end up being stuck in some kind of "loop" (instructions 2566, 2568, 256a, 256c are being executed repeatadly).

The instructions here are 2-byte sized (compressed), but while executing the `jal` instruction, the CPU saves `pc+4` instead of `pc+2` as a return address, just as if the executed instruction was 4-byte sized  (not compressed). For this reason I decided to rerun the simulation, but this time with a binary, that doesn't contain compressed instructions (remove `c` from `march` in https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/blob/master/litex/soc/cores/cpu/cv32e41p/core.py#L32):
```
    "standard": "-march=rv32i2p0_m    -mabi=ilp32 ",
```
 After this change everything worked fine - I got the bios prompt.

(reading some issues related to OpenHW group cores)

@panantoni01 Hum, strange...
Does it mean there would be a bug with compressed instructions on the 41P?
I haven't seen issues related to it in the openhwgroup repository... :neutral_face:

Thanks for the report and the detailed analysis.

I integrated a workaround/fix in cbac44ac3:
  cpu/cv32e41p: Avoid compressed codegen by default

The issue appears to come from firmware being built with RV32IMC by default. In the failing trace, a compressed `jal` stores `pc+4` instead of `pc+2` as the return address, which skips the caller return-address restore and leaves the BIOS stuck in a loop.

The CV32E41P `standard` variant now builds LiteX software as RV32IM, so GCC will not emit compressed instructions by default. I also kept the previous RV32IMC behavior available  explicitly through the new `imc` variant for anyone wanting to debug or validate the compressed path.

I added a focused regression test for the advertised GCC flags. Full `litex_sim --cpu-type=cv32e41p` boot still needs validation in an environment with `pythondata-cpu-cv32e41p`  installed.

Update: this issue appears to be in the CV32E41P CPU RTL, not in the LiteX wrapper.

The failing case is compressed code, specifically a `c.jal` path where the link address can become `pc+4` instead of `pc+2`. That writes the wrong return address, skips the caller's  `ra` restore, and then execution loops.

The root cause I found is that the RTL computes `is_compressed_o` in `cv32e41p_merged_decoder.sv`, but this signal is not declared as a decoder output port and is not connected in   `cv32e41p_id_stage.sv`. With permissive SystemVerilog handling, `id_stage_i.is_compressed` becomes an implicit undriven net, so the `IMMB_PCINCR` path can use the wrong increment.

The minimal CPU RTL patch that fixes the simulation is:

  ```diff
  diff --git a/rtl/cv32e41p_merged_decoder.sv b/rtl/cv32e41p_merged_decoder.sv
  @@
     input  logic [31:0] instr_rdata_i,
  +  output logic        is_compressed_o,

  diff --git a/rtl/cv32e41p_id_stage.sv b/rtl/cv32e41p_id_stage.sv
  @@
     logic is_clpx, is_subrot;
  +  logic is_compressed;
  @@
         .instr_rdata_i(instr),
  +      .is_compressed_o(is_compressed),
  ```

With this patch, cv32e41p/imc boots in LiteX simulation. However, since the upstream CV32E41P repository is archived, we cannot upstream the CPU RTL fix cleanly. So on the LiteX side  we will keep CV32E41P on the known-good standard RV32IM variant and avoid advertising an imc variant.
This is done with https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/commit/d86a229ea95b70a9c50d914adb28f03205abdd12 and cv32e41p is now also tested back in ci.

title: Data access replay error when crossingType=NoCrossing
body:
I'm using a design based on the SiFive Freedom E310, and I'm seeing 2 cycles of latency between the Rocket core issuing a data access and it appearing on the tile's TileLink interface.

The subsystem's config had RocketCrossingParams with crossingType = SynchronousCrossing(). I switched to NoCrossing to see if this would reduce the latency, and if so by how much.

It did indeed reduce the latency by 1 cycle each way.

However I then noticed an issue where the DCache would issue a valid pulse whilst the TileLink address bus ready was deasserted, then issue an s2_nack back to the rocket core, but when it replayed the access the address would be incorrect.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271666/48977757-b12cf480-f0f4-11e8-96d5-a9b864b7eb30.png)


What happened is an offset calculation has been repeated, corrupting the address. My disassembly looks like so:

```
  1c007e:       10050537                lui     a0,0x10050
  1c0082:       0b050513                addi    a0,a0,176 # 100500b0 <spi_load+0xfe9001e>
  1c0086:       f14025f3                csrr    a1,mhartid
  1c008a:       058a                    slli    a1,a1,0x2
  1c008c:       95aa                    add     a1,a1,a0
  1c008e:       4188                    lw      a0,0(a1)
  1c0090:       8502                    jr      a0
```

The issue is that the ```add a1,a1,a0``` occurs again (the core executes and completes the instruction at 0x1c008c a second time), resulting in an incorrect address in a1.

I've often wondered why the rocket core seems to replay instead of stalling while the various hazards or buses clear. Anyway, does this look like a real bug, and not a configuration issue? Is rocket supposed to work with NoCrossing?

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Make sure there's at least one TL.A register in the NoCrossing case

comments.body: I'm not able to replicate this.  I wrote some identical code, except with different absolute addresses, but with the same code alignment; and I made it so that the first time the `lw` executes, `a.ready` is false, so the nack occurs.  After the pipeline flush, the program resumes executing at the `lw`, as expected; the `add` instruction is not repeated.
If you can send me your waveform, I can perhaps try to understand what's going on.

Thanks for looking into this.

Our design has moved on a little bit since I filed the issue and I haven't been able to recreate the failure.

We are using some custom instruction fetch logic, and I can't rule out the bug being there. I thought I checked it at the time but I didn't store the waveform and I have fixed bugs in the frontend since I filed this. So this is likely a false alarm, sorry about that.

However, I do have an observation about a new issue I now see with the NoCrossing configuration. In trying to recreate this scenario, I configured 4 rocket harts with crossingType=NoCrossing again, and re-run our software. I then noticed the software wasn't progressing and noticed a deadlock of sorts. There is a semaphore register that 3 cores are attempting to claim (atomic swap instruction) and one core trying to release it by writing zero. The system becomes deadlocked because the hart trying to clear the register happens to see a deasserted ready from the tilelink bus every time it attempts the write.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271666/49697107-7607e680-fc07-11e8-8883-88af7ca90074.png)

I notice when we do have SynchronousCrossing set, the valid out from the tile is held until ready is asserted and the transaction is acked by the bus.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271666/49697121-a8194880-fc07-11e8-9945-8f66e997866c.png)

I guess the only way to get this behaviour is with SynchronousCrossing? I presume it'd take changes in the dcache to change the behaviour with NoCrossing?

Thanks again for looking into this. If I do see anything like this in future I'll be sure to save the trace.
Thanks for the update on the previous issue.

Is `SynchronousCrossing(BufferParams.flow)` appropriate for your use case?  This will prevent the livelock issue you observed, but retain the lower latency.

If so, then I think the right thing to do is to add a requirement to the D$ to ban the `NoCrossing` a.k.a. `SynchronousCrossing(BufferParams.none)` case.  I suspect the D$ is not the only component that makes this assumption, but it is a start.  @hcook sound ok?

Nice one, will give this  ago but I reckon it looks good.

Thanks @aswaterman !
